I arrived approximately 20 minutes late due to unavoidable circumstances and apologised immediately. Dr Shamoon agreed to proceed with the consultation, so I believed we would use the remaining time constructively. I initially discussed my ongoing eczema, which has been causing significant physical discomfort and has also impacted my mental health.

When I tried to raise another important issue regarding pain following a recent rhinoplasty, I was abruptly cut off and told I would need to book another appointment because there was “not enough time” and that we should only discuss one issue. The way this was communicated felt dismissive and unnecessarily rude. I was in pain and trying to explain my symptoms, but I was not allowed to finish speaking.

If my lateness was such a concern, I would have preferred to be told at the beginning that the appointment could not go ahead, rather than being seen and then spoken to in a way that made me feel belittled. I ultimately left because I no longer felt comfortable continuing. When I asked for her name, I was told “it’s on the door,” which I found unhelpful and discourteous.

To make matters worse, she followed me outside and stated that she would also be complaining about me for being late. I found this highly unprofessional, particularly in a public setting.

I understand that appointment times are limited and that lateness can affect scheduling. However, that does not justify a lack of empathy or respect.
